goal.what: Whoever builds or changes Turn, a person or an AI, makes it give the person who wants a piece of work what they come for: a work that meets their purpose well, for effort only where only they can decide.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, standard.goal: "Whoever builds or changes the product, a person or an AI, makes it give its users what they come for."

.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:20-21: "turn's user is the person who wants the work. A plugin such as rn connects that person and turn. They get a work that meets their purpose well, and spend effort only where only they can decide."

decisions.decided: The person who wants the work. A plugin such as Rn only connects that person and Turn, so it is not a user of its own.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:3: "What the user and the assistant agreed on 2026-10-31 for the new turn."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:20: "turn's user is the person who wants the work. A plugin such as rn connects that person and turn."

decisions.what: What does that person get, and what do they spend?
decisions.decided: A work that meets their purpose well; they spend effort only on what only they can decide.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:21: "They get a work that meets their purpose well, and spend effort only where only they can decide."

decisions.what: How many objectives, and how is O1 written?
decisions.decided: One objective: "O1: A person who wants a piece of work gets one that meets their purpose well, for effort spent only on what only they can decide." The quality of the work and the person's effort stay in one objective, because they trade against each other, and only key results of one objective carry a priority between them.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, format part priority: "After an objective's key results, for each pair of them that can move against each other, which comes first and why"
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q1 step: "Write it as one sentence: that user as its subject, then a verb, its object and the context it is done in, with no feature or mechanism of the product."

decisions.what: Is a gain left out of O1?
decisions.decided: None. What a caller such as Rn gives saves the person questions, which KR1.2 counts. A template Turn keeps shortens the next run of the kind, which KR1.4 counts.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:48-49: "A caller such as rn may give what it has already settled, so the user is not asked it again."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:94: "Keep the Format and the Checklist as the kind's template, and pass them to designer."

decisions.what: Which key result shows that the work meets the person's purpose?
decisions.decided: KR1.1: the share of requested works that the person puts to use as delivered, with no change that they ask for or make. Higher is better. It counts every sign of failure at once: a change asked for, a change the person makes themselves, a run stopped and a work set aside.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q3 step: "Add the signs of failure, such as giving up, undoing a result or working around the product."

plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q3 step: "Ask whether all the objective's key results could get better while the user still does not get what the objective says"; a count of changes asked for gets better when the person fixes the work themselves or sets it aside.

decisions.what: Which key results show that the person spends effort only on what only they can decide?
decisions.decided: KR1.2: the questions per work that the person judges they did not need to decide; the person judges, as only they know what was theirs to decide. Fewer is better. KR1.3: the time per work that the person spends answering questions and giving approvals. Shorter is better.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q3 step: "Turn each sign kept into one measure, a share, an average per user, a count or a time, and name what it is counted out of."
KR1.2 alone gets better while each needed question costs the person long; KR1.3 holds that.
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q3 grounds: "Make sure the metrics are unambiguous."

decisions.what: Which key result shows how soon the person has the work?
decisions.decided: KR1.4: the time per work from the request to delivery. Shorter is better.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md:32-34 says a new kind's research and the second AI's reading take longer than Claude Code alone, so the wait is a cost the person feels.

decisions.what: Do the key results carry target values?
decisions.decided: No. The fixed paragraph of the format follows them.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, format part okrs: "the fixed paragraph on target values"

decisions.what: Which key result comes first in each pair that can move against each other?
decisions.decided: KR1.1 comes before KR1.2, KR1.3 and KR1.4, each in its own sentence: a question, a minute or an earlier delivery saved is lost when the person cannot use the work as delivered. KR1.2 and KR1.3 come before KR1.4: asking the person what Turn could find out itself delivers sooner, but spends the person's effort, which O1 limits, to save Turn's time, which O1 does not. KR1.2 and KR1.3 move together, so they have no sentence.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q7 step: "Ask which loss keeps the user further from what the objective says."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q7 step: "look first at one that counts how much or how fast beside one that counts how well."

decisions.what: Who takes part in the scenario, and of what kind?
decisions.decided: Two: the person, a person, and Turn, an AI. The internet is no participant: Turn reads it with Claude Code's own tools, so the reading is a step Turn takes, and no step waits on the internet.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, format part participants: "each participant and whether it is a person, an AI or a script."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q4 thinking: "Each one that takes a step is named by its role and its kind"
plugins/turn/README.md:46-48: "Claude Code allowed to search and read the web, with its WebSearch and WebFetch tools. Turn reads the best practice of a new kind on the internet."

decisions.what: How does each diagram name its participants?
decisions.decided: It declares each participant first, with the name and the kind the paragraph gives: Person (person) and Turn (AI).
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q4 step: "Begin each diagram by declaring each participant it uses, with its name and kind as the paragraph gives them."

decisions.what: What does the document leave to the architecture?
decisions.decided: Turn's roles, the design tree, the two phases, the run's files, Lane and the main conversation's relay. The person sees only questions, approvals and the work, so Turn is one box.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q6 step: "Treat the product as one box, and flag each participant named for a piece of it that the user does not run, see or receive."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:136-137: "The design is not given: the user never sees it"

decisions.what: On what piece of work does the scenario run?
decisions.decided: A press release for RoomBook, Northwind's new meeting-room booking app, as in the README's Walkthrough. Turn ships no best practice for a press release, so the run shows the kind's research and approval as well.
grounds: plugins/turn/README.md:74-75: "It is November 2026, and your company, Northwind, launches RoomBook, a meeting-room booking app. You need a press release for it."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ holds architecture, code, meta, prompt, readme, refactor-code, refactor-doc and ux, and no press release.

decisions.decided: "O1: The person gets a press release by answering only their own points".
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q5 step: "write a heading with its ID and a short phrase, the user its subject and its verb active, saying how they reach it."

decisions.what: Where does the scenario start and end?
decisions.decided: It starts with the person's request: "Write a press release for RoomBook, our new meeting-room booking app". It ends with Turn giving the person the press release.
grounds: plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q5 steps: "Write the end first" and "Write as the first message the user's first request to the product."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:47: "turn needs nothing given"

decisions.decided: It names the kind, a press release, and whether it is a document or code, and the person confirms it.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:85-86: "Decide the kind of work from the request, and with it whether the work is a document or code, and confirm them with the user."

decisions.what: What does the person approve for a new kind?
decisions.decided: Turn first reads guides and examples of good press releases on the web, as its own step. It then shows the kind's purpose, its format and its checklist in short, and the person approves them.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:88: "Research the kind's best practice."
.rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:93: "Show the kind's purpose and the conditions to the user for approval"

decisions.what: What is the person asked about this work?
decisions.decided: First its purpose. Then the one point only Northwind decides, the release date, with a recommendation. Then the design, in short lines, for approval.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:105-108: "the goal first: ask the user this work's purpose. ... Ask the user what only they decide, one at a time, with a recommendation." and "Show the user the design, the decisions in short lines, for approval"
plugins/turn/README.md:114-116: "When is the release date? I recommend the 1st of next month"

decisions.what: What happens between the approved design and delivery?
decisions.decided: A loop of Turn's own steps, until every question of the checklist is met: Turn writes the release, then reads it as a reporter would. The person is not asked anything in it.
grounds: .rn/20261013-rebuild/turn-rebuild.md:156-158: "The content phase: what the work says and does. ... until evaluator finds every one good."
plugins/turn/best-practices/ux.json, Q5 step: "Draw a part that repeats as a loop with its condition, holding each step that repeats."
